newsitem.title: USA: Mich. Treasurer says mulling $3.5 bln taxable sale.
newsitem.headline: Mich. Treasurer says mulling $3.5 bln taxable sale.

text.p: Michigan Treasurer Doug Roberts said Friday the state was considering the issuance of around $3.5 billion of taxable pension bonds to fully fund the school employees retirement system.
Roberts said the plan would be similar to one proposed by New Jersey Gov. Christine Todd Whitman in her fiscal 1998 budget, but in the case of Michigan the plan is not driven by budget needs.
He also pointed out that because Michigan's laws and constitution were different than New Jersey's, his office has both legislative and legal issues to deal with before any debt could be issued.

For example, Roberts said bond counsel must become comfortable that the pension debt is not considered state debt, which would necessitate voter approval. He added that legislation would also be needed to implement the plan.
Roberts said the pension bond sale would only be cost-effective for the state if the debt can be sold at an interest rate of less than eight percent.
"If I can't make it work, nothing changes in Michigan," he said.

Roberts said while the structure of the bonds is still under review, they may be backed by annual state appropriations and may use school districts' annual pension contribution of 3.6 percent of their annual payroll to pay debt service.
He added a state authority may also be created to issue the bonds.
